---
title: "Design notes"
---

Why the robot is built the way it is. Not needed at the bench --- useful for
your report, and for anyone changing the design.

## Why an FOC ESC

Several ESC solutions were explored for the FAAV concept:

- **Regular drone ESCs.** Hobbyking 12A and EP Aer11 were tested. Both start
  **losing synchronisation at low speed**, which is a problem for water
  propulsion --- precisely the regime the robot spends most of its time in.
- **FOC ESCs** tend to be more complex and larger. The **G431-ESC1** board is
  favourable and had already been explored in the lab.

That tradeoff --- accepting a larger, more complex driver to get usable
low-speed torque control --- is the reason [Module 3](/sessions/03-esc.qmd)
spends a whole module on the driver.

## Speed ceiling and sensor lag

Maximum speed went from **500 to 1700 rad/s**, enough to drive the wings at
10 Hz, through a combination of sensor and MCU changes documented in
[Module 4](/sessions/04-control.qmd). The remaining constraint is sensor
lag: above 500--600 rad/s, uncompensated lag shows up as high current draw and
noise rather than as a hard speed limit.

Compensation is currently hand-tuned every 100 rad/s with a fitted function
used on the robot. Automating this --- ramping through the speeds while
minimising phase current --- is open work.

## Gearbox corrosion {#gearbox-corrosion}

By default the gearbox on the FAAV4 is not waterproof at all, and it is normal
for it to fill completely with water once submerged. This was considered
acceptable: over more than a year of repeated use in water, including in Lake
Geneva, a gearbox was opened and showed no sign of corrosion.

Proper lubrication --- a mix of
**CorrosionX and white lithium grease** - help with corrosion problems. The practical procedure is in
[Module 10](/sessions/10-waterproofing.qmd).

## Housing material tradeoff

| Foam | Floatability | Absorption | Impact behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Extruded polystyrene | Best, low density | Zero | Brittle; little help damping landings |
| Closed-cell polyethylene | Decent, relatively low density | Light | Compliant; usable as protection |

A multi-material housing has never been built but would likely be better than
either.
